concept.name: Earnings per share
concept.definition: A public company's net profit divided by its number of common shares outstanding, reported as basic EPS on weighted-average shares and as diluted EPS including the potential shares from options, warrants, and convertibles. It is the standard per-share measure of profitability shown on the income statement.
concept.intuition: EPS turns total profit into an amount 'per share of ownership,' making companies of different sizes comparable and forming the denominator of the P/E ratio.
concept.mechanics: Basic EPS divides net income minus preferred dividends by the weighted-average common shares outstanding during the period; diluted EPS assumes conversion of all dilutive securities, adding them to the share count and adjusting income. U.S. companies report both on the face of the income statement.
concept.formula: EPS = (Net income - Preferred dividends) / Weighted-average common shares outstanding.
concept.failure_modes: Buybacks can grow EPS even when total profit stagnates; one-time gains and non-GAAP 'adjusted' figures undermine comparability, and dilution from stock compensation is easy to undercount.
concept.misconceptions: Higher EPS is not automatically value creation - borrowing to repurchase shares raises EPS while raising risk - and EPS ignores how much capital was invested to generate the earnings.
concept.example: A company earning $1 billion with 500 million weighted-average shares reports basic EPS of $2.00; if options add 25 million dilutive shares, diluted EPS is about $1.90.
